Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 29 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS Overview of PM Narendra Modi’s visit to Karnataka on April 15, 2026 On April 15,2026, Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi visited Karnataka, where he inaugurated the Sri Guru Bhairavaikya Mandira at Sri Kshetra Adichunchanagiri in Mandya district (Karnataka) and addressed the gathering. Exam Hint: ✓ What? PM Narendra Modi Visited Karnataka ✓ When? 15 April 2026 ✓ Inauguration: Guru Bhairavaikya Mandira ✓ Where? Karnataka (Mandya – Sri Kshetra Adichunchanagiri) ✓ Highlight: First sitting PM to visit Adichunchanagiri Mutt ✓ Felicitation: Mysuru Peta (traditional royal design) ✓ Agenda: 9-point plan for ‘Viksit Karnataka’ & ‘Viksit Bharat’ ✓ Book Released: Saundarya Lahari and Shiva Mahimna Stotram (with H. D. Deve Gowda). Highlights of the Visit: Prayer: During his visit, he also visited the Jwala Peetha and offered prayers at the Sri Kalabhairava Temple in Jadigenahalli, Karnataka. Inauguration of Guru Bhairavaikya Mandira: During his visit to Karnataka, PM Narendra Modi inaugurated the Guru Bhairavaikya Mandira at Sri Kshetra Adichunchanagiri Mutt, a prominent spiritual and educational centre in Mandya, Karnataka. • In its over 1,800-year history, he became the first sitting Indian PM to visit the institution, marking a significant milestone for its followers. • Sri Guru Bhairavaikya Mandira is a memorial dedicated to Sri Sri Sri Dr. Balagangadharanatha Mahaswamiji, the 71st Pontiff of Sri Adichunchanagiri Mahasamsthana Math. • Built in the traditional Dravidian architectural style, it stands as a tribute to his life and legacy, serving both as a place of reverence and a source of inspiration for future generations. • Sri Sri Sri Dr. Balagangadharanatha Mahaswamiji was widely respected for his lifelong dedication to social service, establishing numerous educational and healthcare institutions. Felicitation: PM Narendra Modi was felicitated with a Mysuru Peta crafted from Mysuru and Benaras silk, adorned with a string of pearls and small pendants. This design of the peta was traditionally worn by the erstwhile King Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar of Mysuru. Unveils Nine-Point Agenda: PM Modi presented a nine-point, citizen-driven development agenda for achieving “Viksit Karnataka” and “Viksit Bharat,” highlighting the importance of sustainability, cultural values, and collective responsibility while addressing a gathering at Sri Adichunchanagiri Mutt in Karnataka. • The agenda urged citizens to conserve water (especially in the Cauvery basin), promote tree plantation under Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam, maintain cleanliness, support local products (Vocal for Local), encourage domestic tourism, adopt natural farming, follow healthy eating habits including millets, embrace yoga and fitness, and foster a spirit of service (Seva) towards society. Book Release: During the event, PM Narendra Modi jointly released the book titled ‘Saundarya Lahari and Shiva Mahimna Stotram’ along with former PM H. D. Deve Gowda in Mandya (“Sugar City”). About Karnataka: Chief Minister (CM) – Siddaramaiah Governor – Thaawar Chand Ghelot Capital – Bengaluru National Park (NP) – Anshi NP, Nagarhole (Rajiv Gandhi) NP

Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 30 Daily Content PDF MoC&I Notified India’s First Chip Fabrication Plant at Dholera SEZ, Gujarat In April 2026, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoC&I) notified India’s first chip fabrication plant, a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) to be established by Tata Semiconductor Manufacturing Private Limited (TSMPL), a subsidiary of Tata Group, at Dholera SEZ, Gujarat, with a proposed investment of Rs 91,000 crore. • The SEZ is designed to support electronic hardware, software, and Information Technology (IT)- enabled services with enabling infrastructure and a dedicated approval mechanism to streamline operations and logistics. Exam Hints: ✓ What? India’s First chip fabrication Special Economic Zone (SEZ) notified ✓ By Whom? MoC&I ✓ Where? Dholera, Gujarat (Fab SEZ) ✓ Lead Entity: TSMPL ✓ Investment: Rs 91,000 crore ✓ Other SEZ: Micron Semiconductor Technology (Gujarat), Hubballi Durable Goods Cluster (Karnataka), CG Semi (Gujarat) and Kaynes Semicon (Karnataka). About Chip Fabrication Plant: Size: The SEZ covers 66.166 hectares (ha) of land and is designed to strengthen India’s semiconductor ecosystem and import substitution strategy. Policy: The approval follows amendments to SEZ Rules 2006 amended in 2025 to promote semiconductor and electronics investments. Reform: The minimum contiguous land requirement for semiconductor and electronics SEZs has been reduced from 50 ha to 10 ha, easing project establishment. Flexibility: Additional reforms include inclusion of free-of-cost supplies in Net Foreign Exchange (NFE) calculations and permitting Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) sales on applicable duties. Significance: The reforms promote high-value investment and innovation, improve ease of doing business, strengthen India’s semiconductor ecosystem, support integrated manufacturing clusters, and reduce import dependence. Other SEZ Approvals: Micron: Micron Semiconductor Technology India Private Limited was notified for a Semiconductor Assembly, Testing, Marking and Packaging (ATMP) unit in Sanand, Gujarat over 37.64 ha with Rs 13,000 crore investment and 20,786 jobs. Hubballi: Hubballi Durable Goods Cluster Private Limited was approved for electronics components manufacturing and services in Karnataka over 11.549 hectares with Rs 100 crore investment and 4,360 jobs. CG & Kaynes: CG Semi Pvt Ltd and Kaynes Semicon Pvt Ltd were approved for Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Testing (OSAT) units in Gujarat and Karnataka with investments of Rs 2,150 crore and Rs 681 crore, creating 1,911 and 2,020 jobs respectively. Outcomes: These SEZ approvals strengthen India’s semiconductor ecosystem, build domestic value chains, generate high-skilled employment, and reduce import dependence. About India Semiconductor Mission (ISM): Launch: It was approved by the Union Cabinet in December 2021, aims to build a strong semiconductor and display ecosystem and position India as a global electronics hub. Outlay: It is supported by an incentive framework of Rs 76,000 crore providing up to 50% fiscal support for silicon fabs, compound semiconductors, assembly, testing, and chip design.

MeitY Constituted AIGEG To Drive AI Governance Strategy of India In April 2026, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), constituted the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance and Economic Group (AIGEG) to strengthen India’s approach towards responsible and inclusive AI development. • This newly formed high-level inter-ministerial body will serve as India’s central institutional mechanism for AI governance policy development and coordination. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Technical Support: As per MeitY official notification, AIGEG will be supported by a Technology and Policy Expert Committee (TPEC). • TPEC has been tasked to offer expert advisory to the AIGEG on global developments, emerging technologies, risks, regulation and other evolving priorities relating to AI policy and governance. Composition: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, MeitY will serve as the chairperson of AIGEG. • Apart from Chairperson, Union Minister of State (MoS) Jitin Prasada, MeitY, will serve as Vice Chairperson of the group, while S. Krishnan Secretary, MeitY has been appointed as the Member Convener. • Other key members of the group include: Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser(PSA) to the Government of India (GoI); Dr. V. About India AI Governance Guidelines: Background: In February 2026, MeitY published the India AI Governance Guidelines to establish a principle-based framework for safe and trusted AI innovation anchored in seven guiding Sutras (including Trust, People First, and Innovation over Restraint). Nature: It is a non-permanent, nominated body with members serving on a rotational basis rather than holding a constitutional post. Difference: Unlike the Deputy Chairman, who is a constitutional position elected by members, Vice- Chairpersons are nominated and serve temporarily. Continuity: The panel ensures uninterrupted functioning of the House and reflects multi-party representation in presiding roles. About Rajya Sabha: Overview: Rajya Sabha is the Upper House of Parliament representing states and Union Territories(UTs), constituted on 3 April 1952 as a permanent legislative body under the Constitution of India. Composition: It has a maximum strength of 250 members, including 238 elected from states and UTs and 12 nominated by the President of India for their expertise in art, literature, science, and social service. Election: Members are elected indirectly by elected Members of Legislative Assemblies (MLAs) through proportional representation using the single transferable vote system. Tenure: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body, not subject to dissolution, with one-third of members retiring every two years and each serving a term of six years. Special Powers: The Rajya Sabha can authorise Parliament to legislate on State List subjects and create All India Services under constitutional provisions. INTERNATIONAL AFFAIRS IMF’s WEO 2026: USA Topped, India Slips to 6th Spot in Global GDP Rankings In April 2026, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) released its latest April 2026 World Economic Outlook (WEO) titled “Global Economy in the Shadow of War”. As per the data, India has slipped from the 4th spot to 6th spot in global Gross Domestic Product (GDP) rankings, despite the country being one of the fastest-growing economies in the world. • The data revealed that India’s economy is projected to reach USD 3.92 trillion in 2025, up from USD 3.5 trillion in 2024, placing it behind the United Kingdom (UK) (USD 4 trillion) and Japan (USD 4.4 trillion). Exam Hints: ✓ What? World Economic Outlook (WEO) 2026: Global GDP Rankings released ✓ Who? IMF ✓ India’s Ranking: 6th spot (USD 3.92 trillion) ✓ Top 3 Economies: The USA (ranks 1st, USD 39 trillion); China (ranks 2nd, USD 27.5 trillion); Germany (ranks 3rd, USD 5 trillion); ✓ Key Reasons: ✓ Currency Depreciation: 88.5 per USD (in 2025) ✓ Base-Year Revision: from 2011-12 to 2022-23 ✓ Decline in nominal GDP: Rs 345.5 trillion ✓ India’s Outlook: USD 6.17 trillion by 2030. Key Findings: Top 3 Major Economies: The latest data estimated that the United States of America (USA) will continue to retain its position in global GDP rankings, with a projected GDP of USD 39 trillion. • It is followed by China (USD 27.5 trillion); Germany (USD 5 trillion). India Fastest-Growing Economy: Despite change in India’s global rankings, the country will continue to be the fastest-growing major economy in the world. • India is expected to reclaim the 4th position by 2027 as its GDP increases to USD 4.58 trillion, and will further overtake Japan by 2028. • As per IMF latest estimates, India’s GDP is estimated to reach USD 6.17 trillion by 2030.
